---
title: "Class 19: The Same Code in Any Dimension"
subtitle: "What carries over from the 1D solver, and the two places it genuinely changes"
format:
  html:
    page-layout: full
    toc: true
---

The flowchart in [Class 15](15_Class.qmd) laid out the one-dimensional solver step by step.
Going to two or three dimensions does **not** add steps to that chart, and it does not
reorder them. The architecture is the same: build the arrays, loop the elements, loop the
quadrature points, scatter, solve.

What changes is what lives *inside* some of the boxes. Most of them scale up without any
new idea --- a longer vector here, a bigger element matrix there. Three of them change in
kind, and those three are what the next few classes are really about.

The column down the middle below is that shared infrastructure, drawn the same way as the
trajectory in Class 15: the steps, the element loop, the quadrature loop. It is the same in
any number of dimensions. **Click any box** and the one-dimensional version of that step
appears on the left and the multidimensional version on the right, tagged as unchanged,
merely larger, or genuinely different.

```{=html}

    max-width:900px;margin:0 auto;color:var(--ink)}
.fw svg{display:block;width:100%;height:auto;border:1px solid var(--faint);border-radius:8px;background:#fff}

.fw .cap b{color:var(--ink)}
.fw .hit{cursor:pointer}
</style>

<div class="fw">
  <svg id="f19" viewBox="0 0 880 1040" role="img"
       aria-label="The one-dimensional finite element trajectory, with the multidimensional counterpart of each step shown alongside"></svg>
  <div class="cap" id="f19cap"></div>
</div>

<script>
(function(){
var SEL=5;
var INK='#18202b',GREY='#6b7684',FAINT='#dfe4ea',ACC='#b8322a',BLUE='#2b5fa8',
    PAPER='#f8f9fb',AMB='#ffe9a8',GRN='#2f7d4f',S='';

function esc(t){return String(t).replace(/&/g,'&amp;').replace(/</g,'&lt;');}
function R(x,y,w,h,o){o=o||{};
  S+='<rect x="'+x+'" y="'+y+'" width="'+w+'" height="'+h+'" rx="'+(o.r||0)+'" fill="'+(o.f||'none')+
     '" stroke="'+(o.s||'none')+'" stroke-width="'+(o.sw||1)+'" opacity="'+(o.o===undefined?1:o.o)+'"'+
     (o.d?' stroke-dasharray="'+o.d+'"':'')+'/>';}
function T(x,y,t,o){o=o||{};
  S+='<text x="'+x+'" y="'+y+'" font-size="'+(o.s||12)+'" fill="'+(o.f||INK)+
     '" text-anchor="'+(o.a||'start')+'" font-weight="'+(o.w||400)+
     '" font-family="'+(o.m?'ui-monospace,Menlo,monospace':'system-ui,sans-serif')+
     '" letter-spacing="'+(o.ls||0)+'">'+esc(t)+'</text>';}
function L(x1,y1,x2,y2,o){o=o||{};
  S+='<line x1="'+x1+'" y1="'+y1+'" x2="'+x2+'" y2="'+y2+'" stroke="'+(o.s||INK)+
     '" stroke-width="'+(o.sw||1.3)+'"'+(o.d?' stroke-dasharray="'+o.d+'"':'')+'/>';}
function C(x,y,r,f,st){S+='<circle cx="'+x+'" cy="'+y+'" r="'+r+'" fill="'+f+'"'+
     (st?' stroke="'+st+'" stroke-width="1.8"':'')+'/>';}
function AR(x1,y1,x2,y2,col){col=col||INK;
  var dx=x2-x1,dy=y2-y1,m=Math.sqrt(dx*dx+dy*dy)||1,ux=dx/m,uy=dy/m;
  L(x1,y1,x2-ux*5,y2-uy*5,{s:col,sw:1.5});
  S+='<path d="M'+x2+' '+y2+' L'+(x2-ux*6-uy*3)+' '+(y2-uy*6+ux*3)+
     ' L'+(x2-ux*6+uy*3)+' '+(y2-uy*6-ux*3)+'Z" fill="'+col+'"/>';}
function GR(x,y,nx,ny,c,o){o=o||{};
  for(var i=0;i<ny;i++)for(var j=0;j<nx;j++)
    R(x+j*c,y+i*c,c,c,{f:o.f||'none',s:o.s||GREY,sw:o.sw||0.8});}
function down(x,y1,y2,col){col=col||INK;
  L(x,y1,x,y2-7,{s:col,sw:1.5});
  S+='<path d="M'+(x-4.5)+' '+(y2-7)+' L'+x+' '+y2+' L'+(x+4.5)+' '+(y2-7)+'Z" fill="'+col+'"/>';}

/* ---- the 1D counterpart, drawn in the left panel ---- */
function d1mesh(x,y){ var x0=x+10,x1=x+230,yy=y+66;
    L(x0,yy,x1,yy,{sw:1.5});
    for(var e=0;e<=4;e++){var xx=x0+(x1-x0)*e/4; L(xx,yy-8,xx,yy+8,{sw:1.5}); C(xx,yy,3.4,INK);}
    T(x+120,y+108,'IEN(a,e) = a + p·e',{a:'middle',s:11.5,m:1});
    T(x+120,y+126,'a formula',{a:'middle',s:10.5,f:GREY}); }


function d1id(x,y){ var x0=x+10,x1=x+230,yy=y+66;
    L(x0,yy,x1,yy,{s:FAINT,sw:1.5});
    for(var A=0;A<7;A++){var xx=x0+(x1-x0)*A/6;
      if(A===6) C(xx,yy,4.2,'#fff',ACC); else C(xx,yy,3.4,INK);}
    T(x+120,y+104,'one prescribed node',{a:'middle',s:10.5,f:GREY}); }


function d1room(x,y){ GR(x+42,y+34,6,6,13,{f:'#fff'}); GR(x+132,y+34,1,6,13,{f:'#fff'});
    T(x+120,y+126,'small and dense',{a:'middle',s:10.5,f:GREY}); }


function d1elem(x,y){ var x0=x+18,x1=x+108,yy=y+52;
    R(x0-6,yy-11,x1-x0+12,22,{r:4,f:AMB,o:.55});
    L(x0,yy,x1,yy,{sw:1.5}); C(x0,yy,3.4,INK); C(x1,yy,3.4,INK);
    AR(x+118,yy,x+150,yy,GREY);
    var p0=x+160,p1=x+226;
    L(p0,yy,p1,yy,{sw:1.5}); C(p0,yy,3.4,ACC); C(p1,yy,3.4,ACC);
    T((p0+p1)/2,yy+22,'ξ ∈ [−1,1]',{a:'middle',s:10.5,f:ACC});
    T(x+120,y+110,'one coordinate',{a:'middle',s:10.5,f:GREY}); }


function d1quad(x,y){ var x0=x+30,x1=x+210,yy=y+48;
    L(x0,yy,x1,yy,{sw:1.4});
    for(var q=0;q<3;q++){var xx=x0+(x1-x0)*(q+0.5)/3;
      S+='<path d="M'+(xx-4)+' '+(yy-4)+' L'+(xx+4)+' '+(yy+4)+' M'+(xx+4)+' '+(yy-4)+
         ' L'+(xx-4)+' '+(yy+4)+'" stroke="'+ACC+'" stroke-width="1.8"/>';}
    T(x+120,y+86,'n points',{a:'middle',s:11,f:GREY});
    R(x+76,y+98,88,26,{r:4,f:PAPER,s:FAINT});
    T(x+120,y+115,'J = dx/dξ',{a:'middle',s:12,m:1});
    T(x+120,y+140,'a number',{a:'middle',s:10.5,f:GREY}); }


function d1grad(x,y){ R(x+34,y+40,172,40,{r:5,f:PAPER,s:FAINT});
    T(x+120,y+65,'dN/dx = (dN/dξ) / J',{a:'middle',s:12.5,m:1});
    T(x+120,y+104,'divide by one number',{a:'middle',s:11,f:GREY});
    T(x+120,y+128,'the chain rule, once',{a:'middle',s:10.5,f:GREY}); }


function d1ke(x,y){ GR(x+70,y+44,2,2,24,{f:'#fff'}); GR(x+134,y+44,1,2,24,{f:'#fff'});
    T(x+120,y+124,'(p+1) × (p+1)  —  2×2 at p = 1',{a:'middle',s:10.5,f:GREY}); }


function d1neu(x,y){ var x0=x+30,x1=x+210,yy=y+58;
    L(x0,yy,x1,yy,{sw:1.5});
    for(var e=0;e<=3;e++) L(x0+(x1-x0)*e/3,yy-7,x0+(x1-x0)*e/3,yy+7,{sw:1.4});
    C(x0,yy,5,ACC); AR(x0-26,yy,x0-7,yy,ACC);
    T(x+120,y+102,'h enters at a single point',{a:'middle',s:11,f:GREY});
    R(x+52,y+114,136,26,{r:4,f:PAPER,s:FAINT});
    T(x+120,y+131,'F[0] += h',{a:'middle',s:12,m:1}); }


function d1scat(x,y){ GR(x+36,y+30,2,2,17,{f:AMB}); AR(x+80,y+47,x+106,y+47,GREY);
  GR(x+118,y+13,5,5,17,{f:'#fff'});
  T(x+120,y+128,'IEN says which global function,',{a:'middle',s:11,f:GREY});
  T(x+120,y+144,'ID says which equation',{a:'middle',s:11,f:GREY}); }
function d1solve(x,y){ GR(x+44,y+26,5,5,13,{f:PAPER}); T(x+120,y+59,'=',{s:15,a:'middle'});
  GR(x+132,y+26,1,5,13,{f:PAPER});
  T(x+120,y+128,'a small dense system \u2014 numpy solves it',{a:'middle',s:11,f:GREY});
  T(x+120,y+144,'without you thinking about it',{a:'middle',s:11,f:GREY}); }
function d1draw(x,y){ var x0=x+22,x1=x+218,yb=y+100,d='';
  for(var k=0;k<=40;k++){var t=k/40; d+=(k?' L':'M')+(x0+(x1-x0)*t)+' '+(yb-54*Math.sin(Math.PI*t));}
  S+='<path d="'+d+'" stroke="'+ACC+'" stroke-width="1.9" fill="none"/>';
  for(var A=0;A<=4;A++){var t2=A/4; C(x0+(x1-x0)*t2,yb-54*Math.sin(Math.PI*t2),2.6,INK);}
  T(x+120,y+128,'a curve, sampled inside each element',{a:'middle',s:11,f:GREY}); }

/* ---- the 2D counterpart, drawn in the detail panel (about 240 wide) ---- */
function d2mesh(x,y){ var c=26,gx=x+58,gy=y+14;
  GR(gx,gy,4,3,c,{f:'#fff'});
  for(var i=0;i<=3;i++)for(var j=0;j<=4;j++) C(gx+j*c,gy+i*c,3,INK);
  T(x+120,y+118,'IEN is read from the mesh file,',{a:'middle',s:11,f:GREY});
  T(x+120,y+134,'not computed from a formula',{a:'middle',s:11,f:GREY}); }
function d2id(x,y){ var c=26,gx=x+58,gy=y+14;
  GR(gx,gy,4,3,c,{f:'#fff'});
  for(var i=0;i<=3;i++)for(var j=0;j<=4;j++){
    if(j===0) C(gx+j*c,gy+i*c,4.2,'#fff',ACC); else C(gx+j*c,gy+i*c,3,INK);}
  L(gx,gy,gx,gy+3*c,{s:ACC,sw:2.6});
  T(x+120,y+118,'a set of mesh edges Γg is prescribed,',{a:'middle',s:11,f:GREY});
  T(x+120,y+134,'not a single point',{a:'middle',s:11,f:GREY}); }
function d2room(x,y){ GR(x+22,y+10,11,11,7.6,{f:'#fff'}); GR(x+118,y+10,1,11,7.6,{f:'#fff'});
  for(var i=0;i<11;i++)for(var j=0;j<11;j++) if(Math.abs(i-j)<2||Math.abs(i-j)===3)
    R(x+22+j*7.6+1,y+10+i*7.6+1,5.6,5.6,{f:BLUE,o:.35});
  T(x+120,y+118,'the same array, far larger and',{a:'middle',s:11,f:GREY});
  T(x+120,y+134,'almost all zero — so, sparse',{a:'middle',s:11,f:GREY}); }
function d2elem(x,y){ var qx=x+22,qy=y+16;
  S+='<path d="M'+qx+' '+(qy+14)+' L'+(qx+62)+' '+qy+' L'+(qx+78)+' '+(qy+60)+
     ' L'+(qx+10)+' '+(qy+70)+'Z" fill="'+AMB+'" opacity=".55" stroke="'+INK+'" stroke-width="1.4"/>';
  AR(x+110,qy+36,x+142,qy+36,GREY);
  R(x+156,qy+8,62,62,{f:'#fff',s:ACC,sw:1.5});
  T(x+187,qy+86,'(ξ,η) ∈ [−1,1]²',{a:'middle',s:10.5,f:ACC});
  T(x+120,y+134,'a quadrilateral, possibly distorted',{a:'middle',s:11,f:GREY}); }
function d2quad(x,y){ var c=46,gx=x+74,gy=y+8;
  R(gx,gy,c*2,c*2,{f:'#fff',s:INK,sw:1.4});
  for(var i=0;i<3;i++)for(var j=0;j<3;j++){
    var xx=gx+c*2*(j+0.5)/3, yy=gy+c*2*(i+0.5)/3;
    S+='<path d="M'+(xx-4)+' '+(yy-4)+' L'+(xx+4)+' '+(yy+4)+' M'+(xx+4)+' '+(yy-4)+
       ' L'+(xx-4)+' '+(yy+4)+'" stroke="'+ACC+'" stroke-width="1.6"/>';}
  R(x+58,y+108,124,28,{r:4,f:'#fffaf2',s:ACC});
  T(x+120,y+127,'DF = ∂x/∂ξ   (2×2)',{a:'middle',s:12,m:1,f:ACC});
  T(x+120,y+152,'n×n points; the Jacobian is a matrix',{a:'middle',s:10.5,f:GREY}); }
function d2grad(x,y){ R(x+14,y+26,212,46,{r:5,f:'#fffaf2',s:ACC,sw:1.5});
  T(x+120,y+55,'∇ₓN = DF⁻ᵀ ∇_ξ N',{a:'middle',s:14,m:1,f:ACC});
  T(x+120,y+96,'invert a matrix, then transpose it,',{a:'middle',s:11,f:GREY});
  T(x+120,y+112,'at every quadrature point',{a:'middle',s:11,f:GREY});
  GR(x+88,y+124,2,2,16,{f:'#fff'}); }
function d2ke(x,y){ GR(x+48,y+14,4,4,19,{f:'#fff'}); GR(x+136,y+14,1,4,19,{f:'#fff'});
  T(x+120,y+118,'four nodes per quadrilateral,',{a:'middle',s:11,f:GREY});
  T(x+120,y+134,'so 4×4 at degree 1',{a:'middle',s:11,f:GREY}); }
function d2neu(x,y){ var c=30,gx=x+54,gy=y+16;
  GR(gx,gy,4,3,c,{f:'#fff'});
  L(gx,gy,gx+4*c,gy,{s:ACC,sw:3});
  for(var k=0;k<4;k++){var xx=gx+4*c*(k+0.5)/4; AR(xx,gy-22,xx,gy-4,ACC);}
  for(var e2=0;e2<4;e2++) for(var g=0;g<2;g++){
    var xg=gx+e2*c+c*(g+0.5)/2;
    S+='<path d="M'+(xg-3)+' '+(gy-3)+' L'+(xg+3)+' '+(gy+3)+' M'+(xg+3)+' '+(gy-3)+
       ' L'+(xg-3)+' '+(gy+3)+'" stroke="'+GRN+'" stroke-width="1.5"/>';}
  T(x+120,y+124,'a quadrature loop along each face,',{a:'middle',s:11,f:GRN,w:600});
  T(x+120,y+140,'with its own arc-length Jacobian',{a:'middle',s:11,f:GREY});
  T(x+120,y+156,'(which is not det DF)',{a:'middle',s:10.5,f:GREY}); }
function d2scat(x,y){ GR(x+16,y+20,4,4,13,{f:AMB}); AR(x+76,y+46,x+100,y+46,GREY);
  GR(x+112,y+6,8,8,13,{f:'#fff'});
  T(x+120,y+128,'IEN says which global function,',{a:'middle',s:11,f:GREY});
  T(x+120,y+144,'ID says which equation — unchanged',{a:'middle',s:11,f:GREY}); }
function d2solve(x,y){ GR(x+30,y+16,8,8,11,{f:PAPER}); T(x+128,y+66,'=',{s:15,a:'middle'});
  GR(x+140,y+16,1,8,11,{f:PAPER});
  T(x+120,y+128,'the same solve, but sparse — a direct',{a:'middle',s:11,f:GREY});
  T(x+120,y+144,'dense solve stops being affordable',{a:'middle',s:11,f:GREY}); }
function d2draw(x,y){ var gx=x+46,gy=y+18,c=26;
  for(var i=0;i<3;i++)for(var j=0;j<5;j++){
    var v=Math.sin(Math.PI*(j+0.5)/5)*Math.sin(Math.PI*(i+0.5)/3);
    R(gx+j*c,gy+i*c,c,c,{f:ACC,o:0.12+0.5*v,s:'#fff',sw:0.6});}
  T(x+120,y+124,'a surface instead of a curve,',{a:'middle',s:11,f:GREY});
  T(x+120,y+140,'drawn as contours or a colour map',{a:'middle',s:11,f:GREY}); }

/* ---- the eleven steps.  v: 0 unchanged, 1 just bigger, 2 genuinely different ---- */
var ST=[
 {t:'The mesh and the data',        v:1, a:d1mesh,  b:d2mesh},
 {t:'Decide what is unknown',       v:0, a:d1id,    b:d2id},
 {t:'Make room for the big system', v:1, a:d1room,  b:d2room},
 {t:'Look at one element',          v:1, a:d1elem,  b:d2elem},
 {t:'One quadrature point',         v:2, a:d1quad,  b:d2quad},
 {t:'Its spatial gradient',         v:2, a:d1grad,  b:d2grad},
 {t:'The element matrix',           v:1, a:d1ke,    b:d2ke},
 {t:'Boundary terms',               v:2, a:d1neu,   b:d2neu},
 {t:'Add it into the big system',   v:0, a:d1scat,  b:d2scat},
 {t:'Solve',                        v:1, a:d1solve, b:d2solve},
 {t:'Evaluate and draw it',         v:1, a:d1draw,  b:d2draw}
];
var VERD=[{t:'UNCHANGED',f:'#eef3ee',s:'#cfe0cf',i:'#2f7d4f'},
          {t:'JUST BIGGER',f:'#f1f3f6',s:'#dfe4ea',i:'#6b7684'},
          {t:'GENUINELY DIFFERENT',f:'#fbeeec',s:'#f0d4d0',i:'#b8322a'}];

var LX=12, LW=256, BX=284, BW=312, RX=612, RW=256;
var BH=56, GAP=20, CX=BX+BW/2, PH=292;

function loopFrame(x,y,w,h,label,col){ col=col||GREY;
  R(x,y,w,h,{r:9,s:col,sw:1.2,d:'6 4'});
  var lw=label.length*5.6+16;
  R(x+16,y-9,lw,18,{r:4,f:'#fff',s:col,sw:1});
  T(x+16+lw/2,y+3.5,label,{s:9,a:'middle',f:col,w:700,ls:.5}); }

function panel(x,y,title,tag,drawFn,hot){
  R(x,y,LW,PH,{r:9,f:'#fff',s:hot?ACC:FAINT,sw:hot?1.5:1.2});
  R(x,y,LW,34,{r:9,f:hot?'#fffaf2':PAPER}); R(x,y+26,LW,8,{f:hot?'#fffaf2':PAPER});
  L(x,y+34,x+LW,y+34,{s:hot?'#f0d4d0':FAINT,sw:1});
  T(x+12,y+22,title,{s:11,w:700,ls:.8,f:hot?ACC:GREY});
  drawFn(x+(LW-240)/2,y+48);
}

function draw(){
  S=''; var ys=[], y=48;
  T(LX+2,26,'ONE DIMENSION',{s:10.5,w:700,ls:1.4,f:GREY});
  T(BX+2,26,'THE SHARED INFRASTRUCTURE',{s:10.5,w:700,ls:1.4,f:INK});
  T(RX+2,26,'TWO OR THREE DIMENSIONS',{s:10.5,w:700,ls:1.4,f:GREY});

  for(var i=0;i<ST.length;i++){
    if(i===3) y+=26;
    if(i===4) y+=24;
    ys.push(y); y+=BH+GAP;
    if(i===5) y+=16;
    if(i===8) y+=18;
  }
  var totalH=Math.max(y+10, 120+PH);

  loopFrame(BX-8,ys[3]-26,BW+16,(ys[8]+BH+12)-(ys[3]-26),'FOR EACH ELEMENT',GREY);
  loopFrame(BX+2,ys[4]-22,BW-4,(ys[5]+BH+10)-(ys[4]-22),'FOR EACH QUADRATURE POINT',ACC);

  for(var i2=0;i2<ST.length;i2++){
    var st=ST[i2], on=(i2===SEL), vd=VERD[st.v], by=ys[i2];
    R(BX,by,BW,BH,{r:7,f:on?'#fffaf2':'#fff',s:on?ACC:INK,sw:on?2:1.2});
    R(BX,by,4.5,BH,{r:2,f:vd.i,o:on?1:.4});
    C(BX+26,by+BH/2,11.5,on?'#fff':PAPER,on?ACC:FAINT);
    T(BX+26,by+BH/2+4,String(i2+1),{a:'middle',s:11.5,w:700,f:on?ACC:GREY});
    T(BX+48,by+(st.v?24:33),st.t,{s:12.5,w:on?700:600});
    if(st.v) T(BX+48,by+40,vd.t,{s:8.5,w:700,ls:.5,f:vd.i});
    if(i2<ST.length-1) down(CX,by+BH,ys[i2+1]);
    S+='<rect class="hit" data-i="'+i2+'" x="'+BX+'" y="'+by+'" width="'+BW+
       '" height="'+BH+'" fill="transparent"/>';
  }

  var sel=ST[SEL], vd2=VERD[sel.v], hot=(sel.v===2);
  var py=Math.max(44,Math.min(ys[SEL]+BH/2-PH/2, totalH-PH-14));
  L(LX+LW,py+PH/2,BX,ys[SEL]+BH/2,{s:hot?ACC:GREY,sw:1.2,d:'4 3'});
  L(BX+BW,ys[SEL]+BH/2,RX,py+PH/2,{s:hot?ACC:GREY,sw:1.2,d:'4 3'});
  panel(LX,py,'1D — '+sel.t.toUpperCase(),vd2,sel.a,false);
  panel(RX,py,(hot?'2D / 3D — ':'2D / 3D — ')+sel.t.toUpperCase(),vd2,sel.b,hot);

  document.getElementById('f19').setAttribute('viewBox','0 0 880 '+totalH);
  document.getElementById('f19').innerHTML=S;
  document.getElementById('f19cap').innerHTML =
    '<b>Step '+(SEL+1)+', '+esc(sel.t)+' — '+vd2.t.toLowerCase()+'.</b> '+
    (sel.v===2 ? 'One of the three steps that change in kind. Every box above and below it is the code you already wrote.'
     : sel.v===1 ? 'Nothing new to learn here — the same operation on larger arrays.'
                 : 'Identical in both. The bookkeeping does not care how many dimensions you are in.');
}

document.getElementById('f19').addEventListener('click',function(ev){
  var h=ev.target.closest('.hit'); if(!h) return;
  SEL=+h.dataset.i; draw();
});
draw();
})();
</script>
```

## What the picture is telling you

Eight of the eleven steps are either identical or simply larger. You already know how to
write them. Three are not, and they are worth naming before you meet them in code.

**The Jacobian, and spatial gradients.** These two go together. In one dimension the
Jacobian is a single number and the chain rule is a division: $dN/dx$ is
$(dN/d\xi)$ over the Jacobian. In two dimensions it becomes
$\nabla_x N = (DF)^{-T}\,\nabla_\xi N$ --- you invert a matrix and transpose it, at every
quadrature point of every element. Using $DF^{-1}$ instead of $DF^{-T}$ is the single most
common bug in a first 2D code, and on a mesh of rectangles it will not show up, because
$DF$ is then diagonal and the two agree. It only breaks once an element is distorted.

**Neumann boundary terms.** In one dimension the boundary of the domain is two points, and
$h$ enters as one number added to one entry of $\mathbf{F}$. There is no integral. In two
dimensions the boundary is a curve, and $\int_{\Gamma_h} N_A\,h\;d\Gamma$ is a real
integral that needs its own quadrature loop along each boundary face, with its own
arc-length Jacobian --- which is *not* $\det DF$. That machinery has no one-dimensional
counterpart at all, which is why it gets a class of its own.
